lines.text: Movies always show castle moats filled with ferocious man-eating alligators, but why did medieval lords actually build them?
No, they weren't stocked with crocodiles; they were built to stop the deadliest siege tactic in history: mining.
Enemy armies didn't just scale walls with ladders; they dug subterranean tunnels straight under castle foundations.
They propped up the tunnels with timber, set them on fire, and collapsed giant stone towers from below.
A deep moat flooded any underground tunnels with water, drowning enemy diggers instantly.
Moats also prevented heavy battering rams and rolling siege towers from reaching fortress walls.
A simple ditch of murky water defeated the most advanced medieval siege tactics.
